examples.trans: From your own phone? And everyone believed it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В мире всё всегда меняется.
examples.trans: Everything in the world always changes.

examples.text: Строятся и растут новые города.
examples.trans: New cities are built and grow.

examples.text: Рождаются миллионы новых людей.
examples.trans: Millions of new people are born.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('full').

examples.text: Дима, поверь мне, я в полном порядке.
examples.trans: Dima, believe me, I am completely fine.

examples.text: Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: This is a total nightmare!

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'рядок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Подожди, Дима, смотри, я в порядке.
examples.trans: Wait, Dima, look, I am fine.

examples.text: Дима, поверь мне, я в полном порядке.
examples.trans: Dima, believe me, I am completely fine.

examples.text: Я сам решаю, в порядке ты или нет.
examples.trans: I decide for myself whether you are fine or not.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'yourself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лучше я сама ему всё скажу.
examples.trans: It is better if I tell him everything myself.

examples.text: Вика, как ты сама об этом думаешь?
examples.trans: Vika, what do you think about this yourself?

examples.text: Сейчас ваш шеф сам готовить будет!
examples.trans: Right now your chef is going to cook himself!

meanings.en: to decide, to make up one's mind
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'decide', paired with 'решить'.

examples.text: Я сам решаю, в порядке ты или нет.
examples.trans: I decide for myself whether you are fine or not.

examples.text: Сами решайте, что делать.
examples.trans: Decide for yourselves what to do.

examples.text: Мы вместе решаем все вопросы.
examples.trans: We decide all matters together.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'or', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне недавно предложили поработать в России.
examples.trans: I was recently offered work in Russia.

examples.text: Я сам решаю, в порядке ты или нет.
examples.trans: I decide for myself whether you are fine or not.

examples.text: Ничего, мы это уже раньше проходили!
examples.trans: Never mind, we have already been through this before!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нет, друзья, рано вы меня забыли!
examples.trans: No, friends, you have written me off too soon!

examples.text: И сейчас скажешь, что ничего нет?
examples.trans: And now will you also say that there is nothing going on?

examples.text: Нет, я просто решила его проучить.
examples.trans: No, I simply decided to teach him a lesson.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Мы должны всегда идти только вперёд.
examples.trans: We must always move only forward.

examples.text: Я иду домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

examples.text: Он идёт на второй срок.
examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Правильно, лучше всегда спокойно есть дома.
examples.trans: Right, it is always better to eat calmly at home.

examples.text: Иди домой, Витя, до вечера!
examples.trans: Go home, Vitya, until tonight!

examples.text: Так что иди спокойно домой и отдохни.
examples.trans: So go home calmly and rest.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'until', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты уже стареешь, дорогой Витя?
examples.trans: Are you getting old already, dear Vitya?

examples.text: Раньше ты так долго не думал.
examples.trans: Before, you did not take this long to think.

examples.text: Что тебе надо? Ничего, работаем.
examples.trans: What do you want? Nothing, we are working.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'in the evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Отвечай мне быстро и без обмана!
examples.trans: Answer me quickly and without deception!

examples.text: Вечером нас с тобой ждёт серьёзный разговор.
examples.trans: Tonight a serious conversation awaits the two of us.

examples.text: Иди домой, Витя, до вечера!
examples.trans: Go home, Vitya, until tonight!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will see each other', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
examples.trans: Listen, will we see each other this evening?

examples.text: Увидимся завтра!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Хорошо, увидимся на кухне, администратор!
examples.trans: All right, see you in the kitchen, administrator!
